tasks.independentDerivation: Let horizontal distance x and height h obey x²+h²=400. At h=12, x=√256=16 m. Differentiating gives 2x x′+2h h′=0, so h′=−(16/12)·2=−8/3 m/s. The requested downward speed is 8/3 m/s, matching the worked and short answers.
tasks.sourceFidelity: The full source question and worked solution are retained; terminal [3] is omitted. No source diagram is supplied.
tasks.difficultyReason: The student constructs a right-triangle constraint and links its implicit time derivative to the given instantaneous position and rate; this is a routine taught related-rates procedure.

tasks.independentDerivation: For horizontal distance x, tan θ=10/x, so x=10 cot θ. Differentiating in time gives x′=−10 csc²θ θ′. At θ=π/3 and θ′=−π/6, x′=10·(4/3)·(π/6)=20π/9 km/min ≈6.98 km/min. The decreasing elevation makes x increase, so this is the speed. Both native answers agree.
tasks.sourceFidelity: The full source prompt and worked solution are retained with terminal [3] omitted. The personally inspected original shows the same right triangle, horizontal x km, vertical 10 km and observer angle θ; native TikZ preserves those relationships and omits the decorative plane and telescope.
tasks.difficultyReason: The student selects a trigonometric relation from the supplied triangle, differentiates through the changing angle and interprets the negative angular rate; the linked procedures are taught and the diagram scaffolds the model.

representativeAssessment.reason: The tree introduces a fixed-length moving-distance Pythagorean model; the plane introduces a time-varying trigonometric angle model. They differ from each other and from the supplied comparison context of equilateral area, sphere volume, similar-cone volume, conserved-mass differential equation and Newton cooling. This assessment is limited to the supplied comparison context and is not a new census.
